Universal homeomorphism
Definition
Every base change is a homeomorphism on underlying spaces. No isomorphism of structure sheaves is required.
Setting
A universal property holds on the underlying spaces after every scheme base change Y′→YY^{\prime}\to Y.

Quasi-projective
Definition
Of finite type and admitting a relatively ample invertible sheaf, in the Stacks convention. Hoyois Definition 4.35(ii) uses a quasi-compact open immersion into a projective scheme over the base. Over a quasi-compact and quasi-separated base the Stacks criterion gives such a factorization.
Setting
Properties of f ⁣:X→Yf\colon X\to Y with conditions on full inverse images, the diagonal, or all base changes.

                                                            Surjective

                                                            Görtz–Wedhorn, Appendix D

                                                            Valuative (v) topology

                                                            Grothendieck topologies, sites and topoi

                                                            For a map of qcqs schemes Y→XY\to X, test every Spec⁡V→X\operatorname{Spec}V\to X for a valuation ring VV. There must be an injective local map of valuation rings V↪WV\hookrightarrow W and a lift Spec⁡W→Y\operatorname{Spec}W\to Y over XX. For families, work affine locally on the target and take finite affine refinements whose disjoint union passes the test.

                                                            Grothendieck topologies, sites and topoi

                                                            An object UU is weakly contractible if evaluation at UU sends epimorphisms of sheaves of sets to surjections.                                                             Appendix D, equivalent descriptions

                                                            Hypotheses. Fix a prime pp, a bounded prism (A,I)(A,I) and a smooth pp-adic formal scheme XX over Spf⁡(A/I)\operatorname{Spf}(A/I). Use the bounded absolute site of the same XX.

                                                            Spectrality of the Zariski space

                                                            Equivalence · Qcqs scheme ⇔ Spectral space

                                                            Hypotheses. Let XX be a scheme, and equip ∣X∣|X| with its original Zariski topology.

                                                            Grothendieck diagram

                                                            XX is quasi-compact and quasi-separated if and only if ∣X∣|X| is spectral. Affine opens give a quasi-compact basis, sobriety holds for every scheme, and quasi-separatedness is equivalent to quasi-compactness of affine intersections.

                                                            Equivalent categories

                                                            Equivalence · Spectral space ⇔ Coherent locale

                                                            Also involved · Locale, Spectral map

                                                            Hypotheses. Use classical prime ideal separation, spectral spaces with spectral maps, and coherent locales with maps whose inverse image preserves compact opens.

                                                            Grothendieck diagram

                                                            Taking the locale of opens and taking the space of points give mutually quasi-inverse covariant functors between spectral spaces and coherent locales. Passing to frames of opens instead gives a duality. The compact elements of each frame are the quasi-compact opens of its spectrum.

                                                            Quasi-compact opens as a basis

                                                            basis comparison · Qcqs scheme → Qc Zariski basis site

                                                            Hypotheses. Let X be quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Give its quasi-compact opens the induced Zariski coverings.

                                                            Comparison across diagrams

                                                            Affine opens form a basis. Quasi-compact opens are closed under finite intersection, and coverings of such an open have finite subcovers. Restriction to this basis gives the same sheaves as on all opens.

                                                            Open immersion to its open subscheme

                                                            classification · Open immersion → Open subschemes of X

                                                            Hypotheses. Fix a target scheme X. Identify two open immersions into X when their sources are isomorphic over X.

                                                            Comparison across diagrams

                                                            An immersion in this class identifies its source with its open image U equipped with the restriction of the structure sheaf of X. Factorization over X corresponds to inclusion of open subschemes.

                                                            Closed immersion to its closed subscheme

                                                            classification · Closed immersion → Closed subschemes of X, opposite order

                                                            Hypotheses. Fix a target scheme X. Identify closed immersions up to isomorphism of their sources over X. The diagram uses the opposite of the usual inclusion order on closed subschemes.

                                                            Comparison across diagrams

                                                            A closed immersion i determines a closed subscheme with defining ideal ker(𝒪_X → i_*𝒪_Z). Factorization of one closed immersion through another reverses inclusion of their defining ideals. Passing to the opposite order makes the ideal correspondence order preserving.

                                                            A projective compactification gives a relatively ample line bundle

                                                            Implication · Quasi-projective in the open-in-projective sense ⇒ Quasi-projective

                                                            Hypotheses. Let X → S factor through a quasi-compact open immersion into a projective S-scheme.

                                                            Comparison across diagrams

                                                            The projective scheme has a relatively ample invertible sheaf. Its restriction to X remains relatively ample, as seen over each affine open of S. The quasi-compact open immersion and the projective morphism are of finite type.

                                                            Marc Hoyois, Algebraic Geometry, Definition 4.35(ii), the open-in-projective convention · Stacks 07RL · projective implies quasi-projective · Stacks 0B3E · restriction of ampleness along a quasi-compact immersion · Stacks 01VW · finite type with a relatively ample invertible sheaf · Hoyois, Chapter 8, relative/global panel

                                                            Projective compactification over a qcqs base

                                                            Comparison under hypotheses · Quasi-projective ∧ Qcqs target → Quasi-projective in the open-in-projective sense

                                                            Hypotheses. The target S is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The morphism X → S is of finite type with a relatively ample invertible sheaf.

                                                            Comparison across diagrams

                                                            The morphism factors through an open immersion into a projective S-scheme. This open immersion is quasi-compact because X → S is quasi-compact and the projective S-scheme is separated.

                                                            Valuative (v) topology G000024

                                                            For a map of qcqs schemes Y→XY\to X, test every Spec⁡V→X\operatorname{Spec}V\to X for a valuation ring VV.                                                             Valuative (v) topology is coarser than Arc topology T000031

                                                            Hypotheses. The common qcqs ambient category specified in the valuative diagram.

                                                            The valuation test can be expressed as lifting the specialization from the generic point to the closed point after base change to a valuation spectrum. Over a rank-one valuation ring, lifting that pair of points yields an extension of rank one. Thus an arbitrary-rank cover satisfies the rank-at-most-one test.                                                             Fppf topology = Fpqc topology T000006

                                                            Hypotheses. Separated schemes of finite type over a separated Noetherian base S; see individual edge scope.

                                                            Every fppf family is fpqc. For the converse in this finite-type category over a Noetherian base, every source is locally of finite type over the base, hence locally of finite type over its target. The target is locally Noetherian, so the morphism is locally of finite presentation. An fpqc covering family is flat and jointly surjective, hence fppf here.

                                                            Spectrality of the Zariski space T000135

                                                            Hypotheses. Let XX be a scheme, and equip ∣X∣|X| with its original Zariski topology.

                                                            XX is quasi-compact and quasi-separated if and only if ∣X∣|X| is spectral. Affine opens give a quasi-compact basis, sobriety holds for every scheme, and quasi-separatedness is equivalent to quasi-compactness of affine intersections.

                                                            Equivalent categories T000105

                                                            Hypotheses. Use classical prime ideal separation, spectral spaces with spectral maps, and coherent locales with maps whose inverse image preserves compact opens.

                                                            Taking the locale of opens and taking the space of points give mutually quasi-inverse covariant functors between spectral spaces and coherent locales. Passing to frames of opens instead gives a duality. The compact elements of each frame are the quasi-compact opens of its spectrum.

                                                            Coherent locales and bounded distributive lattices, contravariantly T000138

                                                            Hypotheses. Use coherent frames and frame homomorphisms preserving compact elements, or their opposite category of coherent locales. Use bounded distributive lattices and maps preserving the bounds and finite meets and joins.

                                                            Taking the compact elements of a coherent frame and taking the frame of ideals of a bounded distributive lattice are inverse equivalences at the level of frames. Passing to locales reverses arrows.

                                                            Hypotheses. Profinite sets with a fixed strong limit cardinal size bound and finite jointly surjective covering families.

                                                            Hypotheses. Take the base change X=Spec⁡(𝐅p)→Y=Spec⁡(𝐙)X=\operatorname{Spec}(\mathbf F_p)\to Y=\operatorname{Spec}(\mathbf Z) and the maps a(x)=xa(x)=x, b(x)=x+pb(x)=x+p of 𝐀Y1\mathbf A^1_Y.

                                                            The equalizer of ha,hbh_a,h_b on the lisse-étale site of YY is the initial sheaf because a smooth YY-scheme is flat and no nonempty flat YY-scheme maps to the equalizer fibre. After base change, a=ba=b, so the equalizer is represented by 𝐀X1\mathbf A^1_X. The left adjoint induced by the base-change functor sends representables to their base changes and preserves the initial sheaf. It therefore fails to preserve this equalizer, ruling out a geometric morphism induced by that functor.

                                                            Related concepts. Lisse-étale site · Geometric morphism

                                                            Comparison lemma for sites T000152

                                                            Hypotheses. Let u:𝒞→𝒟u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D be continuous and cocontinuous. Require that two arrows with the same image under uu agree after a cover of their common source, and that an arrow u(U′)→u(U)u(U')\to u(U) locally lifts after a cover of U′U' in 𝒞\mathcal C. Require every object of 𝒟\mathcal D to have a cover by objects in the image of uu.

                                                            The morphism Sh⁡(𝒞)→Sh⁡(𝒟)\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D) obtained from the cocontinuous functor uu is an equivalence.

                                                            Hypotheses. Let SS be a scheme, with the big site formed in a fixed size convention.

On the big étale site use the geometric points of all objects T→ST\to S, evaluating the stalk after restriction to TeˊtT_{\text{ét}}.                                                             Hypotheses. Fix a small category 𝒞\mathcal C. Let JJ be a Grothendieck topology on 𝒞\mathcal C, and order topologies by inclusion of covering sieves.

                                                            Big crystalline site
                                                            Definition
                                                            An object is a divided-power thickening U↪TU\hookrightarrow T over (S,ℐ,γ)(S,\mathcal I,\gamma) with an SS-map U→XU\to X. A cover is a Zariski open cover of TT, with UU and its divided-power structure restricted along each open immersion.
                                                            Setting
                                                            A prime pp, a divided-power scheme (S,ℐ,γ)(S,\mathcal I,\gamma) over 𝐙(p)\mathbf Z_{(p)}, and an SS-scheme XX over V(ℐ)V(\mathcal I) with pp locally nilpotent on XX.
                                                            Relations

                                                            Small crystalline site
                                                            Definition
                                                            In the big crystalline site take the full subcategory on thickenings (U,T,δ)(U,T,\delta) with U→XU\to X an open immersion. Covers arise by restricting a thickening to an open cover of TT.

                                                            Forget the base

                                                            Relative prismatic site ⇢ Site or topos comparison Absolute prismatic site

                                                            Hypotheses
                                                            Fix a prime pp, a bounded prism (A,I)(A,I) and a smooth pp-adic formal scheme XX over Spf⁡(A/I)\operatorname{Spf}(A/I). Use the bounded absolute site of the same XX.
                                                            Statement
                                                            Send a relative object (A,I)→(B,IB)(A,I)\to(B,IB) with Spf⁡(B/IB)→X\operatorname{Spf}(B/IB)\to X to the same prism over XX, forgetting the map from (A,I)(A,I). Any absolute cover of the resulting object lifts to a relative cover by composing the structure map from (A,I)(A,I). The forgetful functor is cocontinuous and therefore gives a geometric morphism from the relative to the absolute topos.

                                                            Qcqs scheme
                                                            Definition
                                                            The scheme is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Equivalently, it has a finite affine open cover and intersections of affine opens are quasi-compact.

                                                            Bounded distributive lattice
                                                            Definition
                                                            A lattice with least and greatest elements and distributive finite meets and joins. Its ideal completion is a coherent frame. Its prime spectrum carries the basic opens consisting of prime ideals missing a given element.

                                                            Spectrality of the Zariski space

                                                            Qcqs scheme ⇔ Equivalence Spectral space

                                                            Hypotheses
                                                            Let XX be a scheme, and equip ∣X∣|X| with its original Zariski topology.
                                                            Statement
                                                            XX is quasi-compact and quasi-separated if and only if ∣X∣|X| is spectral. Affine opens give a quasi-compact basis, sobriety holds for every scheme, and quasi-separatedness is equivalent to quasi-compactness of affine intersections.
                                                            Primary references
                                                            Stacks 094L · Lemma 28.2.4 · Stacks 01KO · affine intersection criterion · Stacks 08YG · definition of a spectral space

                                                            Equivalent categories

                                                            Spectral space ⇔ Equivalence Coherent locale

                                                            Hypotheses
                                                            Use classical prime ideal separation, spectral spaces with spectral maps, and coherent locales with maps whose inverse image preserves compact opens.
                                                            Statement
                                                            Taking the locale of opens and taking the space of points give mutually quasi-inverse covariant functors between spectral spaces and coherent locales. Passing to frames of opens instead gives a duality. The compact elements of each frame are the quasi-compact opens of its spectrum.
                                                            Primary references
                                                            Hochster, Prime ideal structure in commutative rings (1969) · The patch topology in univalent foundations · Blechschmidt, Generalized spaces for constructive algebra · Hochster, Prime ideal structure in commutative rings, Theorem 6 · Stacks 08YG · definition of a spectral space · Bezhanishvili & Melzer, Algebraic frames in Priestley duality, Corollary 5.9, with the categories of §2. Spectral spaces with spectral maps are dual to coherent frames with compact-element-preserving frame maps.

                                                            T000136
                                                            Profinite patch topology

                                                            Patch space ⇒ Implication Profinite space

                                                            Hypotheses
                                                            Let XX be spectral and consider XpatchX_{\mathrm{patch}}, on the same underlying set.
                                                            Statement
                                                            The patch topology is quasi-compact Hausdorff. Its generators are clopen and finite intersections form a clopen basis, so the patch space is totally disconnected and hence profinite.
                                                            Primary references
                                                            Stacks 0901 · constructible topology of a spectral space · Stacks 08ZY · characterization of profinite spaces · Dickmann, Schwartz & Tressl, Spectral Spaces, Theorem 1.3.14. For every spectral space the patch space is Boolean, hence compact Hausdorff with a clopen basis.

                                                            T000137
                                                            Compact elements and ideal completion

                                                            Coherent locale ⇔ Equivalence Bounded distributive lattice

                                                            Hypotheses
                                                            Use coherent frames and frame homomorphisms preserving compact elements, or their opposite category of coherent locales. Use bounded distributive lattices and maps preserving the bounds and finite meets and joins.
                                                            Statement
                                                            Taking the compact elements of a coherent frame and taking the frame of ideals of a bounded distributive lattice are inverse equivalences at the level of frames. Passing to locales reverses arrows.
                                                            Primary references
                                                            Banaschewski, Radical ideals and coherent frames, §1 · Blechschmidt, Generalized spaces for constructive algebra · Hochster, Prime ideal structure in commutative rings, Theorem 6 · Bezhanishvili & Melzer, Algebraic frames in Priestley duality, Remark 5.21. The compact elements form a bounded distributive lattice, and its ideal frame reconstructs the coherent frame.

                                                            T000138
                                                            Hochster realization

                                                            Spectral space ⇔ Equivalence Prime spectrum of a ring

                                                            Hypotheses
                                                            Work in classical set theory. Consider a topological space XX and commutative rings with identity, allowing the zero ring.
                                                            Statement
                                                            XX is spectral if and only if it is homeomorphic to Spec⁡(A)\operatorname{Spec}(A) for some commutative ring AA. The equivalence concerns existence of a realization as a topological space.
                                                            Primary references
                                                            Hochster, Prime ideal structure in commutative rings (1969) · Stacks 08YF · spectral spaces and the constructible topology · Hochster, Prime ideal structure in commutative rings, Theorem 6 · Stacks 08YG · definition of spectral space

                                                            T₁ condition ⇔ Equivalence Profinite space

                                                            Hypotheses
                                                            Let XX be spectral, with its original topology.
                                                            Statement
                                                            XX is T1T_1 exactly when it is profinite. In this case the original topology is also Hausdorff and agrees with the patch topology.

A space is Boolean exactly when it is spectral and all its points are closed.

                                                            fppf\mathrm{fppf}==fpqc\mathrm{fpqc}

                                                            Fppf == Fpqc

                                                            Every fppf family is fpqc. For the converse in this finite-type category over a Noetherian base, every source is locally of finite type over the base, hence locally of finite type over its target. The target is locally Noetherian, so the morphism is locally of finite presentation. An fpqc covering family is flat and jointly surjective, hence fppf here.

                                                            T000006 · Stacks 022C · fppf covers are fpqc · Stacks 01T8 · local finite type over the target · Stacks 01T6 · local Noetherianity of schemes locally of finite type over the base · Stacks 01TX · local finite presentation over a locally Noetherian target

                                                            Fpqc ⟶\longrightarrow Canonical

                                                            Every representable restricts from a representable fpqc sheaf on the big site. The indicated full category is closed under fibre products over its objects, so the sheaf condition applies to its fpqc covering families and their overlaps. The canonical topology contains every such covering sieve.

                                                            Diagram layout and sources

                                                            The 28 comparison relations use straight shafts. The layout leaves 2 interior crossings, shown with a gap in the lower stroke; no shaft enters a label rectangle. Long arrows are retained when the reference lists a direct comparison. On small screens the relation list and scrollable diagram offer the same entries.

                                                            The placement balances crossings, label clearance and separated ports, using a fixed embedding so the diagram does not move during exploration. For alternative approaches see Sugiyama, Tagawa and Toda on layered drawings and Gansner et al. on directed graph drawing.

                                                            Conventions, points and corrections to the source

                                                            For the finite-type comparison fix a separated Noetherian scheme S. The objects are separated S-schemes of finite type. The flat-chain definitions also make sense on the big category of schemes over S, after the usual size choice; on the finite-type category use the generating families that lie there. The fpqc comparison with the canonical topology follows from descent on the big site, applied to those families. “Finer” means containing more covering sieves, not necessarily strictly more.

                                                            A sieve on X is a collection of arrows into X closed under precomposition. A Grothendieck topology specifies which sieves cover, with the maximal sieve covering and with covering preserved under pullback and transitivity. A generating family stands for the sieve it generates. A join is the smallest topology containing all its listed generators. For a fixed underlying category, finer topologies impose more sheaf conditions.

                                                            In the point descriptions, an affine S-scheme P is local for a topology if every map P → X lifts to one member of each covering family of X. The associated fibre functor uses the filtered colimit over finite-type factorizations, as in Gabber–Kelly, Theorems 2.3 and 2.6. These test objects concern the big finite-type site; small-site points, such as the geometric points of the small étale site, are a different assertion. An absolutely integrally closed domain is integrally closed in an algebraically closed fraction field.

                                                            The passports correct the Zar join, the finite symbol, the cdf point and the nontrivial-extension condition for ℓdh\ell\mathrm{dh}. The étale and smooth nodes represent the same topology. A missing arrow does not establish incomparability.

                                                            Valuative and pro-étale topologies

                                                            Valuative comparison

                                                            On quasi-compact, quasi-separated schemes, every arrow sends a covering family for the source topology to a covering family for the target topology.

                                                            fpqc\mathrm{fpqc}⟶\longrightarrowvv

                                                            Fpqc ⟶\longrightarrow Valuative (v)

                                                            After base change to Spec⁡V\operatorname{Spec}V, a faithfully flat cover lifts the specialization from the generic point to the closed point. A valuation-ring extension dominating that lifted specialization gives the required square. For general families use an affine-local standard fpqc refinement.

                                                            T000029 · Stacks 0ETA · valuation lifting and comparison with fpqc and ph

                                                            ph\mathrm{ph}⟶\longrightarrowvv

                                                            Ph ⟶\longrightarrow Valuative (v)

                                                            Given a proper surjection, choose a point over the generic point after base change to Spec⁡V\operatorname{Spec}V. Extend the valuation to the residue field of the chosen point and use the valuative criterion of properness. Zariski covers already satisfy the valuation test.

                                                            T000030 · Stacks 0ETA · valuation lifting and comparison with fpqc and ph

                                                            vv⟶\longrightarrowarc\mathrm{arc}

                                                            Valuative (v) ⟶\longrightarrow Arc

                                                            The valuation test can be expressed as lifting the specialization from the generic point to the closed point after base change to a valuation spectrum. Over a rank-one valuation ring, lifting that pair of points yields an extension of rank one. Thus an arbitrary-rank cover satisfies the rank-at-most-one test. See Proposition 2.1 and Corollary 2.5 of Bhatt–Mathew.

                                                            T000031 · Bhatt–Mathew, The arc-topology · Rydh, Submersions and effective descent of étale morphisms

                                                            Noetherian comparison and the strict refinement

                                                            For f:Y→Xf:Y\to X between qcqs schemes with XX Noetherian, ff is a vv-cover if and only if it is an arc-cover. The Noetherian hypothesis allows testing the vv condition on discrete valuation rings. On the separated finite-type site over a separated Noetherian scheme, the classical hh generators already compare with vv by the Noetherian submersiveness criterion.

                                                            For a valuation ring VV with 0⊊𝔭⊊𝔪V0\subsetneq\mathfrak p\subsetneq\mathfrak m_V, the affine map below is an arc-cover by Corollary 2.9. It fails the vv test on the identity of Spec⁡V\operatorname{Spec}V. The spectrum of a local valuation extension is connected, so a lift must land in one summand. The localization summand omits the closed point and the quotient summand omits the generic point.

                                                            Spec⁡(V𝔭)⨿Spec⁡(V/𝔭)⟶Spec⁡V\operatorname{Spec}(V_{\mathfrak p})\amalg\operatorname{Spec}(V/\mathfrak p)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}V

                                                            Bhatt–Mathew, The arc-topology · Rydh, Submersions and effective descent of étale morphisms

                                                            Affine inverse limits and arc descent

                                                            For affine schemes over an affine target, a standard vv-cover is a directed inverse limit of affine sources whose maps to that target are hh-covers (equivalently, one can use ph covers). This is the precise affine comparison behind the phrase “pro-hh”.

                                                            For a finite ring Λ\Lambda, bounded constructible derived categories of étale Λ\Lambda-sheaves satisfy arc descent. In particular, X↦RΓ(Xeˊt,Λ)X\mapsto R\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}},\Lambda) satisfies arc descent on qcqs schemes. By Definition 2.14 and Proposition 2.19 of Bhatt–Mathew, f:Y→Xf:Y\to X between qcqs schemes is an arc-cover exactly when every qcqs base change f′f' is surjective and every subset UU of its target with (f′)−1(U)(f')^{-1}(U) quasi-compact Zariski open is Zariski open. The resulting open UU is quasi-compact by surjectivity.

                                                            Stacks 0EVM · affine inverse limits of h and ph covers · Bhatt–Mathew, The arc-topology

                                                            The small pro-étale site and Henselian lifting

                                                            The objects of XproeˊtX_{\mathrm{pro\acute{e}t}} are weakly étale schemes over XX, and its coverings are fpqc families of those objects. A morphism f:Y→Xf:Y\to X is weakly étale when both ff and Δf:Y→Y×XY\Delta_f:Y\to Y\times_XY are flat. Every étale morphism is weakly étale, since its diagonal is an open immersion.

                                                            The small étale site includes into the small pro-étale site and induces a morphism of topoi in the direction shown below. This is a comparison of different underlying categories. The arrows in the valuation diagram compare coverings within a fixed category.

                                                            De Jong–Olander prove that weakly étale is equivalent to unique lifting for every Henselian pair (A,I)(A,I) and every commutative square with left arrow Spec⁡(A/I)↪Spec⁡A\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}A. In such a square, a map from Spec⁡(A/I)\operatorname{Spec}(A/I) to YY over a map from Spec⁡A\operatorname{Spec}A to XX extends uniquely to Spec⁡A\operatorname{Spec}A.

                                                            ν:Sh⁡(Xproeˊt)⟶Sh⁡(Xeˊt)\nu:\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{pro\acute{e}t}})\longrightarrow\operatorname{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{\acute{e}t}})

                                                            Bhatt–Scholze, The pro-étale topology for schemes · Stacks 0988 · the pro-étale site · Stacks 099R · comparison with the small étale site · de Jong–Olander, On weakly étale morphisms (2024), Theorem 1

                                                            Relative Frobenius and bounded nilpotence

                                                            For φ:A→B\varphi:A\to B of 𝔽p\mathbb F_p-algebras, Datta–Olander (2026, Theorem 3.23) characterize the bounded-nil formally étale condition by invertibility of the relative Frobenius below. The lifting condition requires a unique lift of every AA-algebra map B→C/IB\to C/I to CC for ideals II whose elements have a uniform nilpotence bound.

                                                            Weakly étale maps satisfy this lifting test because bounded-nil pairs are Henselian. For maps between Noetherian 𝔽p\mathbb F_p-algebras, ordinary formal étaleness already suffices (Theorem 4.6). There are formally étale maps with noninvertible relative Frobenius among non-Noetherian algebras.

                                                            Locally Noetherian⟶\longrightarrowLocally connected

                                                            Locally Noetherian ⟶\longrightarrow Locally connected

                                                            A Noetherian affine open has finitely many irreducible components. Its connected components are unions of classes of those components under the equivalence relation generated by intersection. Each union is open because its complement is a finite union of closed components.

                                                            The pulled-back twisting sheaf is relatively very ample, hence relatively ample by quasi-compactness. A projective morphism is proper and therefore of finite type.

                                                            Projective⟶\longrightarrowProper

                                                            On an affine scheme Spec⁡A\operatorname{Spec}A the closed subsets are V(I)={𝔭:I⊆𝔭}V(I)=\{\mathfrak p:I\subseteq\mathfrak p\}. The closure of 𝔭\mathfrak p is V(𝔭)V(\mathfrak p), so specialization corresponds to inclusion of prime ideals. The principal opens D(f)D(f) are quasi-compact, form a basis and satisfy D(f)∩D(g)=D(fg)D(f)\cap D(g)=D(fg).

                                                            Every scheme is sober: a nonempty irreducible closed subset has a unique generic point. An affine open meeting that subset meets it densely and gives a generic point by the prime ideal description. Two distinct points have distinct closures, since an affine open containing one and hence all of its generizations reduces the assertion to the affine case. For a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme, the constructible (patch) topology generated by quasi-compact opens and their complements is compact Hausdorff. A subset closed in the patch topology is Zariski closed exactly when it is stable under specialization.

                                                            Counterexamples

                                                            Same topological space, different scheme

                                                            Spec⁡k\operatorname{Spec} k and Spec⁡(k[ε]/(ε2))\operatorname{Spec}(k[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)) each have one point; only the first is reduced. The reduction map is a universal homeomorphism.

                                                            Stacks 01IZ · reduced schemes · Stacks 04DC · universal homeomorphisms

                                                            Separated is not Hausdorff

                                                            The scheme 𝔸k1\mathbb A^1_k is separated over k. Its generic point lies in every nonempty open, so the Zariski space is not Hausdorff.

                                                            Stacks 01KH · separation axioms · Stacks 01II · schemes

                                                            Quasi-affine need not be affine

                                                            The punctured affine plane U=𝔸k2∖{(0,0)}U=\mathbb A^2_k\setminus\{(0,0)\} is quasi-affine. Its global ring is k[x,y]k[x,y], by intersecting k[x,y]xk[x,y]_x and k[x,y]yk[x,y]_y in k(x,y)k(x,y). The canonical map to its global spectrum omits the origin and is not an isomorphism.

                                                            Stacks 01P5 · quasi-affine schemes · Stacks 01KX · the punctured affine plane

                                                            Quasi-separated need not be separated

                                                            Glue two copies of 𝔸k1\mathbb A^1_k along D(t)D(t) by the identity. Their intersection is affine, and the finite affine cover makes the scheme quasi-separated. On the product of the two charts over k, the diagonal is the affine diagonal with the origin removed, so it is not closed.

                                                            Stacks 01KH · separation axioms

                                                            Connected need not be irreducible

                                                            Spec⁡(k[x,y]/(xy))\operatorname{Spec}(k[x,y]/(xy)) is the union of two closed affine lines meeting at the origin. Each line is connected, hence their union is connected.

                                                            Stacks 004S · connected spaces and their components

                                                            Reduced need not be normal

                                                            The local ring at the origin of Spec⁡k[t2,t3]\operatorname{Spec}k[t^2,t^3] is a domain but does not contain the element t, which is integral over it. Thus the cusp is reduced and not normal.

                                                            Stacks 033H · normal schemes

                                                            Finite type need not be finite presentation

                                                            Let A=k[x1,x2,…]A=k[x_1,x_2,\ldots] and I=(x1,x2,…)I=(x_1,x_2,\ldots). The closed immersion Spec⁡(A/I)→Spec⁡A\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)\to\operatorname{Spec} A is of finite type, but I is not finitely generated, so this morphism is not of finite presentation.

                                                            Stacks 01TO · morphisms of finite presentation · Stacks 01T0 · morphisms of finite type

                                                            Flat alone need not imply open

                                                            Spec⁡ℚ\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Q → Spec⁡ℤ\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z is flat by localization. Its image is the generic point, which is not open.
